predecessors.name: Mughal Empire
predecessors.text: Quetta, Mastung and Pishin, taken from the Mughal governor of Kandahar

successors.name: Islamic Republic of Pakistan
successors.text: the Kalat country and Makran, incorporated into West Pakistan on 14 October 1955

ledger.x: 1666: Mir Ahmad Khan I founds the Khanate of Kalat.
Mir Ahmad I (1666-1695) 'took Quetta, Mastung, and Pishin from the Mughal governor of Kandahar'.
Samandar Khan (1697-1714) 'expanded to Karachi; the Mughals gave him the port'.
Abdullah Khan (1716-1731) 'extended the state to Bandar Abbas'.
1734: Nader Shah gives Kacchi to Mehrab Khan ('Nader Shah gave Kacchi to Mehrab Khan (1734-1749) as compensation for his father's death').
Nasir Khan I (1749-1794) 'conquered Khash, Bampur, Qasr-e Qand, and Zahedan'.
ledger.cp: local rulers of Persian Baluchistan (page silent)

ledger.x: 1758: Nasir Khan declares independence after the Marathas expel the Afghans from Punjab; Ahmad Shah Durrani besieges Kalat 'for about 40 days and failed to take it'.

1758: peace. Afghan forces besieged Kalat and 'both sides agreed to peace'; by the Treaty of Kalat Nasir Khan 'remained governor and acknowledged Ahmad Shah's overlordship', exempt from annual tribute but supplying men.
Early 19th century: the khanate 'lost much of its territory to Qajar Iran and the Emirate of Afghanistan' (no years on the page).
13 November 1839: the British storm Kalat ('Siege of Kalat (13 November 1839)'; 'Kalat city was sacked by the British').
Karachi: no page opened dates the loss of the port Samandar Khan received.
1877: the Baluchistan Agency is established 'following the 1876 treaty'; its territories included areas 'acquired by lease or otherwise brought under direct British control'.
Kharan separates: 'Kharan became a separate princely state between the 1931 and 1941 censuses' (the Agency page lists Kharan State and Las Bela State with Kalat as princely states in 1941).
14 October 1955: the Khanate of Kalat ends, merged into West Pakistan.

wars.name: Durrani siege of Kalat
wars.outcome: Ahmad Shah besieged Kalat about 40 days and failed; Nasir Khan acknowledged Durrani overlordship, free of tribute.

wars.name: Battle of Kachhi
wars.outcome: Abdullah Khan was killed; Nader Shah later gave Kacchi to Mehrab Khan.

wars.name: Siege of Kalat (1839)
wars.outcome: 13 November 1839: Kalat sacked by the British.

wars.name: Kalat accession revolt
wars.outcome: The Khan's brother led a revolt against accession; the Pakistan Army suppressed it.

certainty.note: A tribal confederacy's reach across Balochistan: no page opened gives a boundary, and the 1835 infobox area is a claim.
The Iran frontier was demarcated in 1896 and is sharp from then; the internal frontiers with the Agency districts and the feudatory states stay soft.
